correctness.rationale: The de Bruijn relation gives H(b_n)=b_n^p L(b_n^p) ~ n and n/b_n^2 -> 0. For p<2 Potter bounds control the truncated variance by nA^2/b_n^2 plus a constant times the Cesàro weighted tail U(A); independent Doob L2 yields a vanishing centered truncated maximal p-moment. Eventual almost increase gives a uniform comparison L(b_n^p)<=K L(|X|^p) above the truncation, so the normalized total tail p-moment vanishes; von Bahr--Esseen and Doob Lp (or the L1 triangle bound) handle the tails. Conversely, failure of quasi-increase selects u_m<v_m with L(u_m)/L(v_m)>=m^3, and regular variation yields n_m~u_m L(u_m), b_{n_m}^p~u_m, and n_m/(m v_m L(v_m))=O(1/m). Symmetric independent rare-spike rows have Cesàro weighted mass exactly 1/m and vanishing occurrence probability, but their normalized maximal p-moments are at least (1+o(1))L(u_m)/(mL(v_m))>= (1+o(1))m^2. The explicit L>=1 example is slowly varying because its logarithm has derivative O(t^-1/2) in t=log(e+x), and peak/trough ratios diverge.

originality.rationale: The 2022 source leaves the p-mean upgrade open; the author answered its monotone-weight case in a 2023-online paper. The final claim is not that covered positive answer, but an exact universal function-class characterization for all positive locally regular slowly varying weights. The primary follow-up Theorem 4.1 only assumes increasing L >= 1, Theorem 3.1 gives per-array tail conditions, and Example 4.2 only disproves removal of the hypotheses through a weight decreasing to zero. The new necessity mechanism works for every non-almost-increasing L, even for L >= 1 and finite-support row variables. Targeted searches of equivalences, broader conditions, and exact aliases found no dominating theorem; monotone-envelope/Orlicz literature remains a material residual risk.
residual_risks: The positive direction can be recovered from general tail-sufficiency theorems after verifying their hypotheses, so only the complete function-class iff and its all-non-quasi-monotone counterexample mechanism are claimed as an advance.

value.rationale: The original source posed the weighted Cesàro weak-law to p-mean upgrade, and the author’s follow-up proved the monotone-weight positive case while exhibiting one decreasing-weight obstruction. The new statement gives the exact sharp boundary on the weight itself: eventual almost increase is sufficient for every independent triangular array and is necessary through a systematic symmetric finite-support construction for every weight outside the class. It also finds a nonmonotone weight bounded below by one where the upgrade fails, clarifying precisely why the published monotonicity condition can be weakened but not discarded. This is a natural complete structural classification, not an arbitrary numeric slice or merely another sufficient condition.
